figure: Figure 10.1 (TP / PP / DP, three stacked panels)
issue: The in-figure color key 'weights (blue)' is honored only in panel A. In panel B the model's layers are drawn as unpatterned white sub-boxes, and in panel C the model is drawn as the orange 'full model (replica)' GPU box; neither B nor C contains any blue. A color reader applying the legend expects the model/weights to be blue in all three panels, so the key is inconsistent with 2 of 3 panels. (The grayscale note disclaims the key as 'redundant, not load-bearing', which protects grayscale legibility but does not fix the key as a color reference.)
evidence: Legend row: 'weights (blue)' with a blue diagonal-hatch swatch. Panel A: the 'one layer's weight matrix W' bar is blue diagonal-hatched (matches). Panel B: inner boxes labeled 'layers 1-8 / 9-16 / 17-24' are white with no hatch and no blue. Panel C: boxes labeled 'full model (replica)' are orange cross-hatched (the GPU fill), with no blue anywhere in the panel.
acceptance_test: Either (a) render the model content with the blue 'weights' hatch in all three panels, or (b) extend the legend with an explicit 'model/layer (white)' entry and a 'model-as-GPU-box (orange)' note, or (c) reword the legend so 'blue' is scoped to panel A only. After the change, a reader using the legend must not be able to look for blue in panels B or C and find none.

figure: Figure 11.1 (Discrete vs continuous batching, Orca-style slot diagram)
issue: The bottom in-figure annotation 'new sequences (green) snap into freed slots' conflicts with both the legend and the drawing. The legend defines green as 'admission event (backfill)' (a thin one-step tick), and in the right (continuous) panel every green mark is a thin tick sitting between two blue 'sequence in flight' blocks; the new sequence's actual decode is the blue block that follows the tick. Calling the green 'new sequences' lets a reader infer that the green tick IS the new sequence (i.e., that a backfilled sequence occupies only one step), which is false.
evidence: Top legend: green hatched swatch = 'admission event (backfill)'; blue solid = 'sequence in flight'. Right panel rows are of the form [blue][green tick][blue][green tick][blue]. Bottom green annotation: 'new sequences (green) snap into freed slots'.
acceptance_test: Reword the bottom annotation to match the legend and the drawing, e.g. 'a freed slot is backfilled at the green admission tick; the new sequence then runs as the following blue block'. After the change, no reader can conclude from the figure that a backfilled sequence's decode is the green tick.

figure: Figure 11.2 (Serving = four separable concerns, not a stack)
issue: Border style is used to encode membership in the canonical baseline, but the encoding is contradicted by the drawing. The caption states 'the canonical baseline uses the first three' and then attaches the rule '(dashed border = not in the canonical baseline)' to resource specialization (box 4). Yet only box 1 has a solid border; box 2 (STATE MANAGEMENT) has a dashed border and box 3 (REUSE) a dash-dot border. A reader applying the caption's rule would misclassify boxes 2 and 3 as outside the baseline, even though the caption says they are in it.
evidence: Caption: '...the canonical baseline uses the first three; resource specialization joins when the workload outgrows a node (dashed border = not in the canonical baseline; see "When to Disaggregate", §11.3).' Drawing: box 1 = solid purple border; box 2 = dashed red border; box 3 = dash-dot green border; box 4 = dashed orange border.
acceptance_test: Make border style encode baseline membership consistently: solid border on the three in-baseline concerns (1, 2, 3) and a dashed border only on the out-of-baseline one (4); OR delete the parenthetical 'dashed border = not in the canonical baseline' and instead put an explicit 'not in canonical baseline' tag on box 4. After the change, no reader can infer from border style that box 2 or box 3 is outside the baseline.

figure: Figure 11.3 (P/D disaggregation: two cases, two different KV links)
issue: In case B the number of GPU squares per host does not match the '8× H100 host' labels nor the 'square = one GPU' convention stated in case A. Case A is internally consistent (4 hatched prefill squares + 4 blue decode squares = 8 under one '8× H100 host'). Case B labels both the prefill host and the decode host '8× H100 host', but the prefill box shows only 4 (at most) hatched squares and the decode box shows 4 blue squares, i.e. not 8 each, so a reader counting squares gets 4+4=8 total for two 8-GPU hosts.
evidence: Case A note: 'square = one GPU (hatched = prefill)'; case A drawing = 2×2 hatched + 2×2 blue under '8× H100 host'. Case B drawing: prefill box labeled '8× H100 host' contains a 2×2 (or 2×1) hatched grid; decode box labeled '8× H100 host' contains a 2×2 blue grid.
acceptance_test: In case B, draw 8 squares per host (matching the '8× H100 host' labels and the case-A 'square = one GPU' rule), or add an explicit 'schematic, not to scale' note to case B, or scope the 'square = one GPU' convention to case A only. After the change, the square count in each box must equal the GPU count in its host label (or be explicitly marked non-to-scale).
